findings.claim: Subscription-model execution has two active authorities: Lattice installs a private sibling model-runner whose Google route is obsolete, while field-survey independently carries working Antigravity, Grok, Claude, and Codex transports.
evidence: axis/tools/model-runner/axis_model_runner/adapters.py binds Google to the retired gemini CLI
counterevidence: The common journal, checkpoint, and bounded-process mechanisms are already shared through axis-model-runner.
Lattice already owns durable invocation identities, manifests, attempts, leases, and runtime receipts.
findings.failure_mode: A provider can be operational in one project and unavailable in Lattice, while route isolation, model selection, credentials, failures, and provenance silently diverge between implementations.
findings.consequence: The multilingual runner can falsely stop at a nonexistent provider block, public Lattice is not independently installable, and successful project-local calls can bypass the canonical conversational graph and its recovery guarantees.
findings.response: Make Lattice the sole execution authority, preserve an internal mechanism/policy seam, consolidate the strongest provider implementations, route all consumers through immutable Lattice submissions, and retire the sibling package only after independent closure.
findings.broader_investigation_trigger: The duplicated Google transport predicts sibling divergence across Claude, Codex, Grok, journaling, provider qualification, and every direct consumer; the consolidation census therefore covers all providers and callers rather than patching Gemini alone.
